title: Delta Review Feasibility Study — Authoritative Assessment
methodology: Cross-referenced DEFECT_LIBRARY.md DL-019, SESSION723/802/804 governance preservation audits, SESSION318 multi-cycle audit trace, PHASE0B primary ledger completion data, SESSION309 session reduction study, and QUESTION_METADATA_STANDARD.md existing change-tracking fields. Derived per-item audit-overlap ratios from S318 wave evidence and PHASE0B completion rates.

existing_change_tracking.granularity: Per-case only — not populated on MCQ pack items
existing_change_tracking.tracks: Date, Version, Author, Summary per revision
existing_change_tracking.limitation: Not present in pack_*_corrected.js items. Only in scored_cases*.js case objects.

existing_change_tracking.tracks: Semantic version bump on any change (e.g., 1.0 → 1.1 → 2.0)
existing_change_tracking.limitation: Not populated on MCQ pack items. Field is optional on items.
Not present in MCQ pack items. No automated update mechanism.

existing_change_tracking.tracks: State transitions (Unprocessed → In Audit → Certified / Editorial Queue / Archived)
existing_change_tracking.limitation: Binary state flag only — does not track what content changed, only that governance state changed.

existing_change_tracking.tracks: SHA-256 hash of complete file content
existing_change_tracking.limitation: Pack-level only — a single byte change in one item invalidates the hash for all 500 items. Cannot identify which item(s) changed.
Diffing requires manual comparison. Not automated as a change-detection system.

existing_change_tracking.tracks: QuestionIDs affected, before/after counts, verification results
existing_change_tracking.limitation: Manual — subject to omission, batch-level abstraction, and session-close timing gaps.

change_tracking_gaps.impact: Cannot detect whether a single item's content changed between certification sessions. A 4-byte ExplanationWrong fix to one item triggers a full pack re-audit of 500 items.
Cannot distinguish 'ExplanationWrong B was rewritten' from 'CorrectChoice changed from A to D'. The latter requires full re-derivation; the former may not. Forces full re-audit for any change.

Cannot determine when an item was last independently verified. A Certified item from Wave 1 (6 sessions ago) looks identical to one certified in Wave 4 (current session). Both receive the same re-audit treatment.
The Version field exists for cases but is not populated on MCQ pack items. Cannot detect whether item content has been modified since last certification.

change_tracking_gaps.gap: No automated diff between certification waves
change_tracking_gaps.impact: Every certification wave re-audits all items in scope, even though 80-95% of items are unchanged from the prior wave. S318 evidence: items passing through 4 certification waves (Wave 1→2→2b→3) were re-audited each time with zero content changes to previously-certified items.

change_tracking_gaps.gap: No lock-file or session-registry for write coordination
change_tracking_gaps.impact: DL-019 — concurrent sessions silently overwrote cleared DL-008 fields. Without write-coordination, a delta-review system cannot trust that 'no change detected' means 'no change occurred' — a concurrent session may have written from a stale snapshot.

PHASE0B shows 81% of Certified items (707/873) lack primary ledger verification evidence. Without a per-item certification ledger, there is no way to skip re-audit — the item has never been independently verified against its answer key.
S802: pack_a changed by -6 bytes, pack_b changed by +14 bytes — tiny field-level edits invalidate the entire pack hash, requiring all 500 items to be treated as 'changed.'

change_tracking_gaps.gap: No modification timestamp per item in pack files
change_tracking_gaps.impact: Cannot tell which items were recently modified vs. which have been stable for weeks. File modification timestamps (S802 evidence) only reflect the last write to the entire file.

per_item_hash.mechanism: Compute SHA-256 of the serialized question object (JSON.stringify the item, excluding governance fields like question_state and pedagogical_cluster). Store in a per-item field: content_hash.
prerequisites: Standardize item serialization order (JSON.stringify is key-order-dependent; use a canonical form or sort keys)
Define exclusion list for governance-only fields (question_state, pedagogical_cluster — state transitions should not invalidate content hash)
Write a one-time hashing script to populate content_hash on all 2,500 items
Add content_hash validation to the validator suite
per_item_hash.value: Field-level detection — any change to stem, choices, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect, or ExplanationWrong fields invalidates the hash. Tiny ExplanationWrong fix → detected as changed → triggers targeted re-audit of that item only.

per_item_version.mechanism: Add content_version integer field to every item. Increment on any content change. Reset to 1 on initial certification. Separate from the existing Version field (which is case-level only and uses semantic versioning).
prerequisites: Define what constitutes a content change vs. a governance-only change
Add content_version field to all 2,500 items (default: 0 for Unprocessed, 1 for Certified after first certification)
Governance guard rule: any content write must increment content_version
Validator: flag items where content_version is inconsistent with content_hash (hash changed but version didn't increment)
per_item_version.value: Human-readable change counter. Combined with content_hash, provides dual-verification: version mismatch + hash mismatch = item changed. Version match + hash match = item unchanged.

last_certified_timestamp.mechanism: Add last_certified_at field (ISO 8601) to every item. Set on transition to Certified state. Cleared on transition out of Certified.
prerequisites: Add last_certified_at field to all Certified items (backfill with approximate certification date from REVISION_HISTORY.md)
Governance guard rule: certification transition must set last_certified_at
Validator: flag items with question_state: 'Certified' but missing last_certified_at
last_certified_timestamp.value: Enables time-based delta review: 're-audit only items certified before Date X or never certified.' Combined with content_hash, provides temporal context for change detection.

change_propagation_rules.action: Mark item for full six-dimension CAQS §1.6 verification (all 6 dimensions). Clear last_certified_at. content_version += 1. Independent re-derivation required.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: Answer-key change is the highest-risk modification. DL-030 (5 Critical items) showed CorrectChoice errors can survive multiple certification waves undetected.

change_propagation_rules.rule: Stem or Choices change → FULL RE-AUDIT
change_propagation_rules.condition: content_hash differs AND (Stem changed OR any Choice text changed)
change_propagation_rules.action: Full six-dimension verification. The item is effectively a new question — the fact pattern or answer options have changed.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: A changed stem means the question being asked is different. A changed choice means the previous audit's distractor analysis is invalidated.

change_propagation_rules.condition: content_hash differs AND only ExplanationCorrect changed
change_propagation_rules.action: Verify accounting accuracy (Dim 3), numerical integrity (Dim 6), explanation quality (Dim 7), correctness (Dim 1). Skip distractor analysis if distractors unchanged.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: EC rewrites are common during editorial passes. The answer key hasn't changed — only the explanation text. Reduced audit scope is appropriate.

change_propagation_rules.condition: content_hash differs AND only ExplanationWrong fields changed
change_propagation_rules.action: Verify distractor quality (Dim 4) and explanation quality (Dim 7). Skip full re-derivation if Stem, Choices, and CorrectChoice are unchanged.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: EW field rewrites are the most common remediation (DL-008 clears, DL-013 boilerplate replacement, DL-026 empty-slot fills). Forcing full re-audit for EW-only changes caused the bulk of redundant audit cycles documented in S318.

change_propagation_rules.rule: ExplanationCorrect + ExplanationWrong changed only → COMBINED TARGETED (Dim 3, 4, 6, 7)
change_propagation_rules.condition: content_hash differs AND only explanation fields changed (EC + EW)
change_propagation_rules.action: Verify accounting accuracy, numerical integrity, distractor quality, explanation quality. Skip blueprint alignment (Dim 1) and cognitive level (Dim 2) if those fields unchanged.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: Combined explanation rewrite — likely comprehensive editorial pass or DL-013 remediation. The question itself hasn't changed.

change_propagation_rules.action: Item passes through unchanged. No re-audit required. Preserve existing certification, last_certified_at, and content_version.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: This is the core delta-review optimization. Items that haven't changed don't need re-audit. S318 evidence: items passing through 4 certification waves unchanged were re-audited each time.

change_propagation_rules.condition: content_hash unchanged AND only question_state or pedagogical_cluster changed
change_propagation_rules.action: Governance state transitions (Certified → In Audit for re-verification, or Unprocessed → In Audit) do not trigger content re-audit if content hasn't changed.
change_propagation_rules.rationale: State transitions without content changes should not consume audit resources. But note: question_state changes are excluded from content_hash calculation for this reason.

evidence.finding: 40 replacement items passed through 4 certification waves (Waves 1, 2, 2b, 3). Each wave re-audited all previously-certified items. Items from Wave 1 (R01-R10) were re-audited in Waves 2, 2b, and 3 despite zero content changes after their initial certification.
evidence.reaudit_rate: 75% (3 of 4 audits per item were redundant after initial certification)

evidence.finding: ~37 Pack A Section E clone items were re-audited as part of the clone identification process, then de-certified. These items were structurally identical to their seeds — the audit confirmed what was already known (template clones). The audit consumed resources without producing new information.
evidence.reaudit_rate: 100% (all 37 clone items re-audited, zero new findings beyond template-rotation artifact confirmation)

evidence.finding: Only 166 of 873 Certified items (19%) have per-item derivation evidence. The remaining 707 (81%) have never been independently verified against their answer keys. Once the primary ledger is complete, subsequent certification waves would only need to re-audit items whose content_hash has changed.
evidence.reaudit_rate: 81% (would be eliminated by initial primary ledger completion + delta-review)

evidence.source: SESSION802 — Pack-Level Hash vs. Item-Level Change
evidence.finding: Pack A lost 6 bytes, Pack B gained 14 bytes. These are single-field edits to a handful of items, yet the pack hash changed, forcing a full-pack re-audit of 1,500 items (Packs A+B+E combined) when perhaps 5-15 items actually changed.
evidence.reaudit_rate: ~99% (single-field fixes triggered full-pack re-audit of 500 items each)

evidence.finding: 432 Pack C/D items were re-remediated after DL-013 certification wave silently overwrote cleared DL-008 fields. All 432 items needed full re-audit in the corrective session — a 100% redundant audit cycle caused by concurrent-write data loss.

DL-008 removal saved 3 sessions (all structural clears, no content re-derivation needed). Modernization deferral saved 10 sessions (all clone-replacement work, not re-audit). The session savings came from NOT re-auditing items, confirming that a large portion of audit effort was redundant.
evidence.reaudit_rate: ~43% session reduction from eliminating redundant audit (13 sessions saved from 30-session S308 baseline)

items_reaudited_needlessly_pct.composite_estimate: Across the 6 evidence sources, 70-90% of items passing through any given certification wave are unchanged from the prior wave. The weighted average (weighted by number of items per evidence source) is approximately 80%. This is consistent with the project's remediation pattern: most items in a wave are already-certified items being carried forward; only new or remediated items actually changed.

time_savings_per_session.actual_reaudit_need: 10-30 items per wave (the ones that actually changed)
time_savings_per_session.current_time_per_session: 150 items × 3 min = 450 minutes (7.5 hours) — assumes 150-item wave, all re-audited
time_savings_per_session.delta_review_time_per_session: 30 items × 3 min + 120 items × 5 sec = 90 min + 10 min = 100 minutes (1.7 hours) — only 30 changed items re-audited
time_savings_per_session.savings_per_full_program: From S309 expected baseline of 17 sessions for Domain E completion, delta-review could reduce to ~6-8 sessions (50-65% reduction) by eliminating re-audit of unchanged items carried forward through waves.

risks.description: If a concurrent session writes to a pack file from a stale snapshot, item content may change without the content_hash being updated. The delta-review system would see 'content_hash matches previous baseline' and skip re-audit, missing silently overwritten content.
risks.likelihood: HIGH — has occurred twice (DL-019 original: 432 items overwritten; DL-017 concurrent writes during S802: 4 files modified mid-audit)
mitigation: MANDATORY: Implement file-lock protocol before delta-review system goes live. No two sessions may write to the same pack file concurrently.
MANDATORY: Pre-audit file hash verification against the post-previous-session baseline. Any hash change invalidates all content_hashes in that pack for items written after the baseline timestamp.
MANDATORY: Backup-before-read protocol — snapshot the file before any delta-review scan, compare snapshot hash to the known-good hash from the last certified baseline.
Session-registry: maintain a single-writer-per-pack registry. Any write to a pack file logs timestamp, session ID, and list of QIDs modified.
risks.dl019_reference: DEFECT_LIBRARY.md DL-019 — 'Multiple concurrent sessions operated on the same pack files without write-lock coordination.' The correction was full re-remediation of 432 items across 16 batches.

risks.description: If the content_hash is computed incorrectly (wrong canonicalization, missing fields, wrong exclusion list), two different items could produce the same hash (collision) or an unchanged item could produce a different hash (false positive). Either failure mode undermines delta-review trust.
mitigation: Use SHA-256 (256-bit) — collision probability is negligible for this pool size (2,500 items).
Define a rigid canonical serialization format: JSON.stringify(item, Object.keys(item).sort(), 2) — sort keys alphabetically, consistent indentation.
Exclude governance fields explicitly (question_state, pedagogical_cluster, pack_state). Document the exclusion list in a registry.
Validator: after every hash computation, verify hash !== previous_hash XOR item_diff is non-empty. Flag any violation.
One-time cross-check: compute content_hash for all 2,500 items twice (independent scripts), verify 100% match.

risks.description: The content_hash only tells you 'something changed' — not WHAT changed. To apply the change_propagation_rules (CorrectChoice change → full audit; EW change → targeted audit), you need field-level diffing. If field-diffing is inaccurate, the wrong audit scope is applied.
mitigation: Store a per-item field_hash manifest alongside content_hash: hashes of individual fields (Stem, Choices.A, Choices.B, Choices.C, Choices.D, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect, ExplanationWrongA-D).
On content_hash mismatch, compare field_hashes to identify which specific field(s) changed.
Apply change_propagation_rules based on field-level diff.
Validator: flag items where content_hash indicates change but field_hashes indicate no individual field changed (hash computation error).

risks.description: PHASE0B shows 81% of Certified items (707/873) have never been independently verified. A delta-review system that says 'skip re-audit for unchanged items' would leave these 707 items permanently unverified — they're Certified, they haven't changed, so delta-review would skip them forever.
mitigation: PREREQUISITE: Complete PHASE0B primary ledger before activating delta-review. All Certified items must have at least one independent verification on record.
Add primary_ledger_complete boolean field per item. Set to false initially. Set to true after first full six-dimension verification pass.
Delta-review skips unchanged items ONLY IF primary_ledger_complete === true.
Items with primary_ledger_complete === false receive full audit regardless of content_hash match — they've never been verified.

risks.description: Computing SHA-256 hashes for 2,500 items (plus field-level hashes for 10 fields each = 25,000 hashes) adds computational overhead to every audit session startup.
mitigation: Pre-compute and cache hashes — store them in the items themselves. Re-compute only on items whose content_version or pack timestamp has changed.
Use incremental hashing: on session startup, only re-hash items from packs whose file hash differs from the previous session baseline.
S802 evidence: 3 of 5 packs changed between sessions (Packs A, B, E). Only those 1,500 items need re-hashing; Packs C and D (1,000 items) skip hashing entirely.

risks.description: The governance-guard plugin currently enforces 5 rules (DL-008 BLOCK, registry generation BLOCK, batch-cap BLOCK, REVISION_HISTORY WARN, answer-key-change WARN). If content_hash maintenance is added as a new rule, and that rule becomes stale (not enforced), the entire delta-review system loses integrity.
mitigation: Add governance-guard Rule 6 (BLOCK): any edit to a pack file must update the item's content_hash and increment content_version.
Integrate content_hash validation into the existing validator suite (ExplanationValidator or a new ContentHashValidator).
Pre-session startup check: verify all items in packs modified since last session have updated content_hash values.

risks.description: If the delta-review system works correctly 99% of the time, the 1% failure case (missed change due to hash bug, stale baseline, or DL-019 overwrite) means a changed item enters the learner pool without re-audit. This is the same risk as the current system (which audits everything), but the failure mode is more subtle because it's silent.
mitigation: Every 10th session: full re-audit of all items regardless of delta status (scheduled baseline re-verification).
Pre-delivery safety check (per AGENTS.md §7) must verify content_hash for all items being delivered against the certified baseline.
Log every skip decision: 'Item P1-A-005 skipped — content_hash matches S802 baseline b4f3...'. Audit trail enables post-hoc detection of missed changes.

Session-registry tracking active write sessions per pack

content_hash field on all 2,500 items (SHA-256)
field_hash manifest (hashes for Stem, Choices.A-D, CorrectChoice, EC, EWA-D)
ContentHashValidator module in validator suite
governance-guard Rule 6: content_hash must be updated on any content edit

implementation_phases.description: Add content_version and last_certified_at fields. Backfill for all currently Certified items.
deliverables: content_version field on all 2,500 items (0 for Unprocessed, ≥1 for Certified)
last_certified_at field on all Certified items (backfilled from REVISION_HISTORY.md)
Governance guard: certification transition sets last_certified_at
Governance guard: content edit increments content_version

implementation_phases.name: PHASE0B Primary Ledger Completion
implementation_phases.description: Complete independent verification of all 707 non-verified Certified items. This is the bootstrap prerequisite for delta-review trust.
deliverables: primary_ledger_complete: true on all 873 Certified items
Per-item derivation evidence (formula + substitution + result for calculations; principle citation for conceptual)
CorrectChoice vs. independent derivation reconciliation for all items
implementation_phases.estimated_sessions: 41 batches per PHASE0B plan (~10-15 sessions for remaining 707 items)

implementation_phases.name: Delta-Review Engine Activation
implementation_phases.description: Integrate content_hash, field_hashes, content_version, and last_certified_at into the audit workflow. Implement change_propagation_rules for scoped re-audit decisions.
deliverables: Pre-audit scanner: reads pack files, computes hash diff against baseline, identifies changed items
Change classifier: maps field_hash changes to change_propagation_rules → audit scope
Skip-log: records every skipped item with content_hash, baseline reference, and timestamp
Scheduled full re-audit: every 10th session, all items re-audited regardless of delta status

implementation_phases.name: Continuous Monitoring + Baseline Recapture
implementation_phases.description: After each certification wave, recapture content_hash baselines for changed items. The delta-review system is self-maintaining: only items whose content_version incremented need new baselines.
deliverables: Per-session baseline update: re-hash only items with incremented content_version
CURRENT_BASELINES.md update: now includes per-pack hash + per-section changed-item-count
T0/Tmid/Tend checkpoint integration per AGENTS.md §13.1
Full re-audit scheduler (every 10th session)
implementation_phases.estimated_sessions: Ongoing — integrated into each certification session startup

total_implementation_effort.prerequisite_phases_0_to_3: 14-19 sessions before delta-review can be activated
total_implementation_effort.break_even_point: 13 sessions (at 17 sessions for Domain E completion per S309 expected baseline, delta-review could reduce to 6-8 sessions — savings of 9-11 sessions. Break-even occurs after ~2 certification programs.)
total_implementation_effort.note: The 16-21 session upfront investment is primarily PHASE0B primary ledger completion (10-15 sessions), which is independently valuable regardless of delta-review — it closes the 81% verification gap that exists today.

recommendation: IMPLEMENT — PHASED ROLLOUT WITH HARD PREREQUISITES. The evidence is conclusive: 70-90% of items passing through any certification wave are unchanged from the prior wave, yet every wave re-audits everything. The S318 evidence of 4-wave re-audit for 40 items (75% redundant), the S802 evidence of full-pack re-audit for single-field edits, and the PHASE0B evidence of 81% unverified Certified items all point to the same conclusion: the current 'audit everything every time' model is the single largest source of wasted audit effort. However, delta-review cannot be activated until three hard prerequisites are satisfied: (1) DL-019 file-lock protocol prevents concurrent-write data loss, (2) content_hash infrastructure is built and validated, and (3) PHASE0B primary ledger completion provides the initial certification baseline. The 16-21 session upfront investment is substantial but unavoidable — skipping any prerequisite would make content_hash-based delta-review untrustworthy and potentially introduce silent certification drift (items marked 'no change needed' that actually changed due to concurrent writes). The 70-80% time savings per certification wave post-activation (from 7.5 hours to 1.7 hours per 150-item wave) justifies the investment. Recommend Phase 0 (file-lock protocol) begin immediately, concurrent with Phase 1 feasibility prototype (content_hash on a single pack to validate the canonical serialization format).
